greeting: Good morning, Bay View. It's a quiet, chilly Tuesday: partly sunny with a high near 40 and light winds. No school for MPS students today (a staff development day), and Thanksgiving break runs Wednesday through Friday, so expect a lot of kids at the parks and the library.

top.title: Thanksgiving forecast: a raw, rainy day by the lake, with highs in the mid-40s
top.dek: Rain chances build Thursday into Thursday night, with gusty northeast winds; little impact expected.
top.body:
The National Weather Service expects a chilly week in Milwaukee, and Thanksgiving itself looks gray and damp along the lakefront. The forecast for Bay View calls for a 40 percent chance of rain on Thursday, mostly cloudy skies, a high near 46 and northeast winds of 15 to 20 mph, gusting as high as 30.

Rain becomes likely Thursday night (a 60 percent chance), though the weather service expects less than a tenth of an inch. Wednesday night brings only a slight chance of rain after midnight, so the trip to Grandma's on Wednesday should be dry, with a high near 43.

Inland, the weather service says some light snow could mix in from Wednesday night through Thursday night, with very light accumulations possible on grassy areas in south central Wisconsin. Forecasters describe the impacts as minimal, and they note the details are still uncertain.

Before then, today is partly sunny with a high near 40 and almost no wind, and tonight turns mostly cloudy with a low around 30. Friday looks drier after a chance of morning rain, with a high near 46 for Black Friday shopping.

spotlight.title: Spotlight: Milwaukee Makers Marketplace
spotlight.dek: A year-round shop where everything is made in Milwaukee, tucked inside the Hide House on Greeley Street
spotlight.body:
Milwaukee Makers Marketplace is a store with one simple rule: the people who stock its shelves made what they sell. It sits in Suite 135 of the Hide House, the former tannery complex at 2625 S. Greeley St. that now holds studios, shops and small businesses, and it carries the work of dozens of local artists and makers: wall art, ceramics, jewelry, candles, apparel and more.

The shop grew out of the Milwaukee Makers Market, the pop-up market run by owner Ryan Laessig. It started in 2017 as a small outdoor market in the Colectivo parking lot at Kinnickinnic and Lincoln avenues, a few blocks away, and grew into a monthly market at venues like Discovery World, American Family Field and The Ivy House. Shepherd Express readers have named it the city's best art and craft fair or makers market five times, most recently in 2025, according to the market's website. In September 2024 Laessig opened the permanent store, telling Radio Milwaukee that spending there goes "right back into the local maker economy." (That Radio Milwaukee piece was written with information from the shop, a sponsor of the station.)

Walk in and you'll find bracelets from Linny's Artsy Fingers, upcycled vintage jewelry from SmitTin, handmade goods from Makery Maven Co. and clothing from Slacker Posse and Giltee Apparel, along with longtime market vendors like Big White Yeti, Nourish Natural Products, Maebel Jewelry and Bay View's own Artery Ink, which is also in the Hide House. A corner of the store doubles as a gallery with rotating exhibitions by local artists. One Bay View-flavored find, according to OnMilwaukee's new food-inspired gift guide: a six-panel cotton cap inspired by the South Shore Farmers Market, made with help from Bay View Threadworks, for $40.

This month has been busy. The gallery opened "Happy Accidents," a first show by an artist named Alexis, on Nov. 14, and the shop thanked Shepherd Express for including it in this year's holiday gift guide. Extended holiday hours run through Dec. 31, though the store is closed on Thanksgiving.

The market side is gearing up, too. Milwaukee Makers Market hosts what it calls Milwaukee's official Shop Small Saturday at Discovery World this Saturday, Nov. 28, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., with more than 50 local small businesses, food trucks and free admission. A holiday market follows there on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Milwaukee Makers Marketplace, 2625 S. Greeley St., Suite 135 (inside Hide House). Holiday hours: Thursday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., Friday and Saturday 11 a.m. to 7 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. (closed Thanksgiving). milwaukeemakersmarket.com; Instagram @milwaukeemakersmarket.

history.title: DeMarinis: Bay View's pizza family since 1949
history.text: In 1949 Vincent and Lucille DeMarinis opened a tavern at Wentworth and Potter. Within two years it was an Italian kitchen, and the DeMarinis name still means pizza in Bay View.
history.body:
Long before Bay View had a dozen pizza choices, it had DeMarinis. According to Milwaukee Record's history of the restaurant, Vincent and Lucille DeMarinis opened a neighborhood tavern on the corner of Wentworth and Potter avenues in 1949. About two years later they turned it into an Italian eatery, and Mama DeMarinis became one of the city's early pizza destinations.

The restaurant stayed in the family for decades. Daughters Josephine and Rosemary eventually took over its operations, and in 1996 the founders' sons, Dominic and Phillip, opened their own restaurant less than two blocks away, Dom & Phil DeMarinis, promising the family's "original recipes." For the next 16 years Bay View had two DeMarinis kitchens, unaffiliated and a short walk apart, and plenty of neighbors had an opinion about which one was the real thing.

Mama DeMarinis closed in 2012. A granddaughter of the founders kept that side of the family going with Little DeMarinis, which opened in 2013 in the basement of Bay View Post 180 and closed in early 2018. That left Dom & Phil's, at 1211 E. Conway St., as the last restaurant carrying the name in the neighborhood.

The original building at 2457 S. Wentworth Ave. found a second life too: since 2014 it has been Goodkind, the restaurant and bar. Dom & Phil's, meanwhile, keeps its menu short and old-school, with only a handful of pizza styles and a Friday fish fry.
